post.caption:
A qubit holds a combination of 0 and 1, but you cannot read a superposition: measuring gives one ordinary answer. The real mechanism is interference, arranging the wrong answers to cancel each other so the right one survives. That only helps for problems with the right structure, and most do not have it. Factoring large numbers does, which is why some encryption is threatened, and simulating molecules does, which is the genuinely useful case. The machines still need extreme cooling and have high error rates.
